transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Lately I keep thinking my clients would be better off if I just weren’t here, and those thoughts about not wanting to wake up are starting to scare me. A colleague at the clinic helped me realize I needed to get some help because I just don't know what to do anymore.
How long have you been feeling this way, and did it start after a specific stressful event or loss?

All of this has been weighing on me for about a month now. It started after a really stressful stretch at work with a cluster of difficult cases and a tense disagreement with my supervisor, which made me seriously question my competence.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or suicidal thoughts before this month, or is this the first time it has happened?

No, this is definitely the first time I've ever felt like this. I’ve never struggled with depression or had thoughts about not wanting to wake up before last month. It’s all completely new and really terrifying to me.
Besides the stress at work, have you also had most days of low mood or lost interest/pleasure in things you usually enjoy, along with changes in sleep, appetite, energy, or concentration?

Yes, I've completely lost interest in playing guitar or seeing friends, and I barely sleep at night, leaving me totally drained of energy. I also have no appetite and have been losing weight, and my brain feels like it's full of mud, making it almost impossible to concentrate during my sessions.
Have these symptoms been improving as the work stress has eased, or have they continued at the same level for most of the past month?

No, they haven't gotten any better at all. They have been consistently weighing me down at this same intense level for about a month now, ever since that rough patch with the difficult cases and the disagreement with my supervisor.
Have you been able to keep up with work and daily responsibilities, or have these symptoms made it hard to function most days?

It has been incredibly hard to function lately. I've started calling in sick or leaving early because I feel too overwhelmed to run my groups, and my paperwork is piling up and getting flagged by my supervisor. At home, I'm ignoring my friends' texts and letting laundry and dishes pile up because I just can't deal with anything.
Have your symptoms been getting better as the work stress has eased, or have they stayed severe even after the stressful situation changed?

No, they haven't gotten any better at all, and they've stayed really severe. Even though I've tried to step back by calling in sick or leaving early, the heavy feelings, guilt, and those dark thoughts have just persisted and actually gotten worse since that initial conflict.
Have your symptoms started to improve now that the work stress has eased, or do they still feel severe and constant even after the stressful situation changed?

No, they haven't improved at all and still feel incredibly severe and constant. I'm still completely overwhelmed and struggling to function, to the point where I have to keep calling in sick because I can't face my responsibilities. It's just been weighing on me continuously like this for the entire month.
Did your symptoms start only after this work stress, or were you already feeling depressed or losing interest before it happened?

No, I wasn't feeling depressed or losing interest in things before all of this happened. Everything only started about a month ago, right after that stressful stretch of difficult cases and the argument with my supervisor. Before those events, I was doing okay and still keeping up with my usual routine.
Have you started to feel any better as the work stress has eased, or do the low mood, loss of interest, and suicidal thoughts stay severe even when things are calmer?

No, they haven't improved at all and remain really severe. Even when work is supposed to be calmer, the loss of interest in my guitar or friends and those thoughts of not wanting to wake up persist every single day and night. It still feels just as heavy as it did when the stress first peaked.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks in the past when you felt depressed or lost interest in things, even without a major stressor?
No, I've never had a period like this before. This is the very first time in my life that I've felt this depressed and completely lost interest in the things I love.
Have the symptoms continued for more than a month after the stressful work situation ended or clearly improved, or are they still directly tied to that stressor?

The symptoms have been going on for about a month now, but the stressful situation hasn't really ended or improved. Instead, the stress has snowballed because I'm falling behind on my work and calling in sick, which makes me feel even more overwhelmed. So it still feels very much tied to that initial stressor and the mess it has caused.
Have your symptoms been present for at least two full weeks most days, even when you are not thinking about the work stressor?

Yes, they've been present almost every single day for about a month now. It’s just this constant, heavy weight that hangs over me all the time, even when I'm trying to distract myself and not thinking about work at all.
Did these symptoms start only after the work stress, and do they seem to be a reaction to that stressor, or did they come on without a clear trigger and keep going независимо of it?

They definitely started right after the intense work stress, especially that disagreement with my supervisor and those difficult cases. At first, it felt like a direct reaction to those events, but now it feels like these feelings have taken on a life of their own. It just weighs me down constantly, regardless of what's happening at the clinic.
Did these symptoms begin within a few weeks of the stressful work event and seem clearly tied to it, or did they start on their own without a clear trigger?

Yes, they started within a week or so of those difficult cases and the disagreement with my supervisor. Those events definitely triggered this downward spiral, and it has been clearly tied to that stress from the very beginning.
Have your symptoms been steadily improving as the work stress settles, or do they still feel severe and unchanged even now?

No, they haven't improved at all and still feel incredibly severe and overwhelming. Even though that initial conflict was about a month ago, I feel like I've just spiraled further, struggling to get through each day, calling in sick, and still dealing with those scary thoughts of not wanting to wake up.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or loss of interest before, even without a major stressor, or is this the first time and it started only after the work conflict?

This is the first time I have ever felt this way. I've never had any episodes of depression or lost interest like this before, and it all only started recently after the stressful events and conflict at my clinic.
Have your symptoms been clearly improving as the work stress settles, or have they stayed severe and constant even when things are calmer?

No, they haven't improved or settled down at all. For the past month, everything has stayed just as constant and severe every single day. Even when things at work are supposedly calmer, the heavy feelings and thoughts don't change.
Have the symptoms started to improve at all as the work stress has eased, or have they stayed just as severe even when the situation is calmer?

No, they haven't improved at all and have stayed just as severe. Even when I am away from the clinic because I've called in sick, the heavy feelings, exhaustion, and those dark thoughts are constant. It has been weighing me down like this for the entire month without any relief.
Have you had any clear relief in your mood and thoughts when you are away from the work stress, or do the depression symptoms stay severe even when the stressor is not present?

No, I don't get any relief when I'm away from work. Even at home during the evenings or on weekends, I just isolate myself in my apartment, staring at the walls and obsessing over my mistakes. The heavy feelings and those thoughts of not wanting to wake up stay just as severe, no matter where I am.
When you are away from the work stress, do your mood and interest improve at all, or do the depression symptoms stay just as severe even in calmer settings?

No, my mood and interest don't improve at all, even when I'm completely away from work. When I try to play guitar or hang out with friends on the weekends, it just feels completely pointless and I can't bring myself to care. I usually just end up sitting alone in my apartment, feeling completely drained and trapped in my own head.
Have these symptoms lasted for less than 6 months, or have they continued for 6 months or longer?
They have lasted for less than six months. All of this started about a month ago, right after that stressful period with the difficult cases and the argument with my supervisor.
Have you had any thoughts of hurting yourself or making a plan to end your life, or are these thoughts more like wishing you would not wake up?

It started out as just wishing I wouldn't wake up, but on my worst day, it went further than that. I actually wrote a note on my phone and started looking up ways to kill myself online. It really scared me, and that's what finally made me reach out to my coworker for help.

Do you feel your symptoms are mainly a reaction to the work stress and conflict, or have they become a full depressive episode with low mood and loss of interest that continues even when the stress is not present?

It definitely feels like a full depressive episode that has taken over everything. Even on my days off or when I'm completely away from the clinic, the heavy mood, constant exhaustion, and complete lack of interest in things like playing my guitar don't lift at all.
Have you ever had a period of at least 4 days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable, needed much less sleep than usual, or felt overly confident or driven?
No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. In fact, it’s been the exact opposite—I just feel completely exhausted, drained, and down all the time.
Have your symptoms stayed severe for at least two weeks after the work stress clearly ended or improved, or do they mainly happen only while the stress is ongoing?
The stress hasn't really ended or improved; in fact, it feels ongoing and has gotten worse because I am falling behind at work. I have been feeling like this constantly for about a month now.
Have you had any time in the past month when your mood and interest improved noticeably, or have the symptoms stayed severe even during days off and away from work?

No, there hasn't been any improvement at all, and it's been constant and severe for the whole month. Even on my days off, I feel completely drained, have zero interest in playing my guitar, and struggle to do basic things like my laundry or dishes. It just feels like a heavy weight that never lifts, no matter what.
Have you thought about acting on these thoughts, or made any specific plan or taken any steps toward harming yourself?

I haven't actually taken any physical steps to hurt myself, but writing that note and looking up methods online felt dangerously close. It terrified me so much that I stopped right there and reached out to my coworker for help. I'm just really scared of how far my thoughts went that day.
Right now, are you having any thoughts of killing yourself, or have you made a specific plan or taken any steps to do it?

Right now, I don't have an active plan to hurt myself, but I still have those thoughts every night that it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up. I'm not looking up ways to do it anymore because that scared me, but those passive thoughts are definitely still there.
Have your symptoms continued for more than two weeks after the work stress clearly ended or improved, or do they mainly happen only while the stress is still going on?

The stress hasn't actually ended or improved because I am still struggling at work, calling in sick, and falling behind on my documentation. These symptoms have been constant and weighing on me every single day for about a month now, ever since that stressful period with the difficult cases and the argument with my supervisor began.
